title: Sim-to-Real Transfer of Robotic Control with Dynamics Randomization
source_version: arXiv v3, 3 March 2018; first submission 2017, related ICRA publication 2018

claims.statement: For Fetch-arm puck pushing, Table II gives the LSTM policy simulation success 0.91 +/- 0.03 over 100 trials and real-robot success 0.89 +/- 0.06 over 28 trials.
claims.locator: Table II and caption; Figure 7 discussion
claims.scope: Reported simulation and Fetch pushing trials; the uncertainty is reproduced as displayed, without assigning an unstated confidence-interval definition.

claims.statement: Table III reports real-robot success 0.89 +/- 0.06 for all randomizations (28 trials), 0.29 +/- 0.11 for fixed action timestep (17 trials), and 0.25 +/- 0.12 with no observation noise (12 trials).
claims.scope: LSTM ablations on this physical pushing task. The comparison does not establish universal transfer performance or an independently rerun experiment.

claims.statement: Dynamics randomization samples episode parameters at rollout start. Mass and damping stay constant within an episode, while action timestep and observation noise vary at each timestep; the setup randomizes 95 parameters.
claims.scope: The described simulation training setup; it does not mean every parameter is resampled at every timestep.
